questions.q: In this lesson's five-link lineage chain, what comes immediately between raw source data and the training run?
options: The deployed instance
The registered model version
The feature-engineered dataset snapshot
The alias assigned to the model
questions.explain: The chain runs raw data → feature-engineered snapshot → training run → model version → deployment. Features sit between raw data and the run that consumes them.

questions.q: What does mlflow.log_input() actually attach to a run?
options: A screenshot of the training script
A structured reference to the dataset used — schema, row count, and source URI — as queryable run metadata
The full contents of the dataset file, copied into the run's artifact store
A plain text comment describing the data informally
questions.explain: log_input() with an mlflow.data dataset object attaches structured, queryable dataset metadata to the run, closing the data-to-run lineage link.

questions.q: How does a model version let you walk backward to the exact training run that produced it?
options: It doesn't — that information is lost once a model is registered
Through the run_id stored on the model version object
By re-running the entire training pipeline from scratch
By checking the model's file creation timestamp
questions.explain: MlflowClient's model version object stores run_id, letting you trace directly back to the run (and from there, the data and code) that produced it.

questions.q: What lineage link does a feature store like Feast primarily own?
options: The connection between a model version and its deployment
The connection between raw source data and the engineered features models train on
The connection between a run and its registered model version
The connection between two different model aliases
questions.explain: A feature store defines and tracks feature transformations, owning the data-to-features link that MLflow itself doesn't track.

questions.q: When does a complete lineage chain typically pay for the effort of maintaining it?
options: Only during model training, never afterward
During incidents and audits, when 'what fed this model' or 'what is this model feeding' needs a fast, certain answer
It never pays off in practice
Only when using MLflow's autolog feature
questions.explain: Lineage is rarely queried day to day; its value shows up when investigating a production issue or responding to an audit request.
